rows.label: Five courses at the 2000 level or above (3-4 credits each), at least four of them in Comparative Literature
rows.note: Counts the five courses: at least four in Comparative Literature, and the fifth in Comparative Literature or a foreign language and literature subject. The board cannot see whether the fifth works in its original language, so the language-course row asks you to confirm that (study-abroad courses are also confirmed by hand).

limits.label: At least four courses in Comparative Literature

rows.label: Confirm the fifth course works with materials in a non-English original language, needs proficiency in it, and is not a lower-level language class
rows.note: Whether a course reads its materials in the original language cannot be seen on the board. It can come from Comparative Literature, a foreign language and literature department or a study-abroad program. Confirm with the director of undergraduate studies.

rows.label: At most one study-abroad course counts toward the minor
rows.note: Study-abroad courses cannot be identified from the catalog.

rows.label: The five courses total at least 15 credits
rows.note: Four counted department courses are at least 12 credits; the fifth course, checked by hand, must bring the total to 15.

rows.label: Each course counted for the minor needs a grade of C or better
rows.note: Grades are not visible to the board.

rows.label: Submit the declaration paperwork to the minor director, then sign off on completion before the deadline in your last semester
rows.note: The form can be filed at any time; the certification meeting has a deadline.
